transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I think occupational health wanted me to come in. I’ve gotten into a pattern where I skip, or sort of push aside, breakfast and lunch when I’m busy with lab runs or exhibition work. Then when I do eat later, I keep it very small and controlled.
Do you find yourself particularly concerned about your weight or shape, or worried about gaining weight even a small amount?
Yes. I do worry about it. If the scale goes up even a little, I get this sudden panic feeling, like I’m losing control or losing the discipline I’ve been trying so hard to keep.
Have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised excessively after eating as a way to control your weight?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think that’s been the main way I deal with it. I mostly just try to keep what I eat small and controlled.
Do you ever find yourself eating a much larger amount of food in a short period than you had planned, and feel like you can’t stop or control how much you eat?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I eat more than I intended, but not like a large amount where I feel unable to stop. It’s more that I’m trying to keep things limited.
Do you ever fast, severely restrict your food intake, or engage in excessive exercise specifically to prevent weight gain or because of your concerns about food and weight?

Yes. I do restrict. I’ll skip or push off breakfast and lunch when I’m busy with lab work, and then when I finally do eat, I keep it very small and controlled. I think that’s part of why occupational health got concerned.
When you're restricting your food intake and keeping your meals very small, are you currently underweight or do you feel that you are already at a weight that's too low?

Yes… I think it’s probably too low now. My clothes are definitely looser, and the numbers on the scale have kept drifting down. Part of me knows that’s concerning, but another part of me sees it as being focused, like I’m keeping things controlled and not letting the chaos at work spill over into my body.

When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you see it differently than what others might see, or do you feel like you still need to lose more weight even though you know you're already underweight?

Yes. When I look in the mirror, especially before going into the lab, I don’t really see myself as thin. I end up focusing on my stomach or my hips, and they look… wrong to me. Like they make me look careless, or not serious enough, even if I know other people might not see it that way.
Even though you know you're already underweight, do you still have a strong desire to lose more weight or believe that losing weight would help you feel better or more in control?

Yes. I do. If the scale goes up even a little, even just a fraction, I get this sharp panic, like I’m losing control or losing the discipline I’ve worked so hard to keep. Losing weight feels like proof that I’m staying in control.
Is your restriction of food mainly driven by a desire to change your body shape or weight, or are you focused on something else when you decide to limit what you eat?

I think it’s partly about my body, but in practice it happens around work. I’ll push breakfast or lunch aside during lab runs or exhibition work, and then when I finally do eat, I keep it very small and controlled. Occupational health noticed and sent me because it’s become a pattern.
Do you follow a strict set of rules or rituals around eating, such as specific portion sizes, types of food, or timing, that you feel you must follow every day?

Yes, I do have rules, I suppose. It’s less like a written list and more this pattern I’ve got into. During lab runs or exhibition work I push breakfast and lunch aside, and then when I finally do eat, I keep it very small and controlled. Occupational health picked up on it because it’s become pretty consistent.
Is your fear of gaining weight or your need to stay thin something that preoccupies your thoughts, even when things at work are calm?
Yes. Even when work is quiet, it’s still there in the back of my mind. If the scale goes up even a tiny amount, I feel this sudden panic, like I’ve lost discipline or control. It’s hard to shake.
